reapack.name: BandSync.lua
reapack.desc: BandSync: record together remotely over a shared folder

version.author: James
version.changelog: First release: publish/open/send/inbox, rooms, lanes, versioned stems, local copies, 24-bit FLAC recording, latency calibration, version checks and updater, AI installer.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Send works per take: sends the active take you picked (send again after picking another); new 'Send all takes' sends every unsent pass, grouped. Sent status tracked per take, so re-recording into a sent item is caught. Selection check compares takes, not counts. Unique take IDs within the same second (fixes a REAPER 'files exist' freeze). Per-song comping style (lanes/takes) detected at publish; takes mode adds incoming takes to the matching item without moving existing audio.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Live sync (replaces Take inbox): every recording goes out by itself when you stop, all passes, printed at the item's exact extent; everyone's takes are rebuilt in the same tracks, lanes and multi-take items; the host shares its existing takes and lanes. Print modes wet (default) / dry / both, with FX-free mirror tracks for wet prints. Takes reprint as new revisions when FX, volume, pan or fades change. The session driver's deletes, moves, trims, lane moves and lane/take choices propagate; 'Take control' passes driving. New Status window with two-way receipts. Fixes: 'dry' prints went through the track (now truly dry), lane play state restore, dry twins on preview upgrade, take deletes in background tabs.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Update (shared-folder installs) also removes actions whose scripts no longer exist, e.g. the old Take inbox.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Status: ages were an hour off in daylight-saving time zones, so everyone showed offline and your own Live sync 'not running'.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Copy/paste, duplicate and split: the copies carried the original's hidden BandSync id, so they never went out (and confused edits/deletes). Copies are now detected and sent as new takes; a split sends the left half as a trim and the right half as a new take.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Live sync never shows a dialog: a newer-BandSync warning used to pause every background script (and Live sync) until clicked. It's now a console line, and the Status window shows a banner.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Deleting something and pasting it back in the same place now syncs again (the 'already sent' guard ignored that the earlier copy was deleted).

version.author: James
version.changelog: The driver's mirrored changes get their own undo point and are logged by name (deleted / moved / now playing). The Status window opens next to the mouse instead of over REAPER's menu bar.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Ownership: claim tracks or song regions so only your edits there propagate; what you can't change is view-only (locked). Recall points at every handover (and by hand): the driver can restore any of them, deleted takes come back. Hold sync. Track mute/solo/name/colour/icon and item mute follow. MIDI takes carry their notes as an editable MIDI copy; note edits sync, and 'Print my MIDI' replaces a print with your own instrument. New BandSync - Panel (needs ReaImGui): everything in one dockable window.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Panel: Stop ends Live sync directly instead of raising REAPER's task-control dialog, and running/stopped shows within seconds. Claimed track and region names keep their case.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Solo edit: check a song out to edit alone through Google Drive (lock with presence, versions with per-track changes, restore any version); wet prints kept beside dry recordings so missing plugins never lose a sound. Live tab: hear each other through REAPER's ReaNINJAM (synced play-along with placeholders on the timeline, live listen, or jam) via a NINJAM server over Tailscale. History & restore tab: every change grouped by person, restore to any point. Take control waits until everyone is in sync. Drum maps translate MIDI drums between VSTs. New sessions print wet + dry.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Live placeholders: each received clip is placed once (no more place/replace loop), and only that person's takes recorded after the live session began replace them. Placeholders appear when the listener disconnects (ReaNINJAM writes its clip log then). Panel: the version banner's Update button no longer raises an ImGui ID error.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Live sync starts Syncthing if it isn't running; the host's Live tab Connect starts the NINJAM server (set its folder once). Placing live placeholders makes one undo point.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Setup guide covers Live (Tailscale share), Solo edit (Google Drive shortcut) and ReaImGui; Solo edit finds Google Drive on macOS by itself

version.author: James
version.changelog: Listen live through SonoBus (peer to peer, low delay, no server, works on Mac); panel Set up list with 'Set up everything I can'; publish/open buttons on non-BandSync projects; one-click installers for Windows (tested) and macOS (untested); Save for the band no longer drops the SonoBus group

version.author: James
version.changelog: Listen live joins with one click and no paste: BandSync writes the band's SonoBus group, password and your name into SonoBus's state. One SonoBus group per band (sonobus.json in the shared folder) instead of per song.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Fixes from the PC-laptop live test: placeholders are replaced only by takes recorded while they were heard, and a newer session's clips replace an older session's; the Play along server field picks up an address the host sets later; Set up shows when REAPER's audio device is closed; the installer reopens itself outside a sandboxed app's shell.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Set up list: Syncthing connected-to-bandmates check and audio-device check; SonoBus set to a steadier jitter buffer (Auto-Increase from 40 ms) and a wired-internet hint; takes go out sooner after you stop; MIDI from a track without an instrument is flagged so receivers know why its print is silent; panel opens inside REAPER's window; installer: works under Windows PowerShell 5.1, downloads the newest release, and its closing list shows only what's left.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Tempo map and markers sync from whoever is driving, and REAPER moves everyone's items by its own timebase; take positions travel in beats; History and recall restores bring back their tempo map. Play along in a second song tab works (ReaNINJAM is moved, not duplicated). MIDI takes print through their instrument and skip the silent dry. Live clip arrival times aren't stored in the project.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Prints contain only the item: a synth routed into the track to record it no longer ends up in the print (it played twice on everyone else's machine).

version.author: James
version.changelog: Restoring a deleted take brings the owner's real item back (not a mirror of their own take); a MIDI copy never reprints without an instrument; old revisions go to _trash instead of being deleted; History shows what really changed on a track, and colour/icon changes (e.g. SWS auto-colour) no longer go out on their own.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Tempo changes no longer make song-long audio drift: band audio follows the beat by position only (moved, never stretched), MIDI parts are reprinted at the new tempo by their owners, and the driver is told which audio takes need re-recording past the change. Fixed: a handover event blocked every later change on receivers.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Tempo changes stretch band audio the way REAPER is set to, piece by piece: in REAPER's default timebase band audio uses REAPER's auto-stretch at tempo changes (unchanged before the change, stretched after it), instead of 0.7.7's position-only. Other timebases are left as the project says.

version.author: James
version.changelog: A new revision of a take plays straight (it was rendered at the current tempo): no stretch left over from the previous print.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Solo edit stops the song tab's Live sync before turning it into the working copy, and Live sync stops by itself in a working copy (it had re-sent the copied media as new takes). Solo edit versions list volume, pan, mute and routing changes, so a mix pass reads as one.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Solo versions leave out the live plug-ins (ReaNINJAM, SonoBus), which only raised load warnings; History shows tempo changes without a bogus -1/-1 time signature.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Together tab: play/record/stop together, notes and likes, live ideas, take back, print MIDI as audio, Solo edit mix, insert/remove bars, dry mode with the sender's plug-ins. Shared mix (volume/pan), reverb tails in wet prints, locked edits snap back, autostart with REAPER, trash cleanup, newest songs first.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Your own takes are yours to move/trim/mute where nobody has claimed. Mix changes made before you joined arrive. Print MIDI as audio keeps the release tail. Panel: Set up only opens for essentials, drum map folds away, bars instead of seconds, Enter posts a note, confirmations for Remove bars and Solo edit mix. History shows volume in dB.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Play/Record together hit the moment on every machine (start/stop cues are checked every 0.25 s; 5 s lead). Insert/Remove bars splits takes that cross the edit point (after asking) and keeps late-arriving takes in place. Notes show on every take of an item. Dry mode names the plug-ins this machine lacks.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Insert/Remove bars: each person splits their own takes, so both parts stay theirs and land on their tracks; MIDI copies are never split (a copy split in two re-sent its notes every 2 s). History restores bring back the tempo/markers an insert left and move MIDI copies with their prints.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Insert/Remove bars splits without losing anything (REAPER's split cuts MIDI notes away; a restore found them gone). History: a 3-minute pause starts a new group, and each group shows its first change. The update banner says when only the open panel is old.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Insert/Remove bars: the trimmed first part of each split take goes out as an edit. A take sent while muted arrives muted. MIDI copies end with their notes, not with the print's reverb tail.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Take back my last take skips the parts an insert/remove split made, and asks with the track and bars.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Panel: the last start/stop together and how close it hit; which take a note goes on; bar numbers everywhere; dry mode says whose part; Remove bars says what it cuts; plainer Live mode texts; Solo edit's folder setting moved below the versions; notes name the track.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Side by side: everyone's normal transport drives everyone (play, stop, record, seeks), followers a set number of bars behind so Play along lets them hear the take in context; the one recording records, the rest listen. Together tab: start from a region, countdown, count-in click, who's ready (Live sync, armed tracks, side by side). Dry mode shows which of the plug-ins you have.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Fix: Live sync's status receipt called the side-by-side helper before it existed (every tick errored on 0.9.0). tests/check_locals.py now catches that.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Side by side: a stop carries the song position, so followers stop exactly where the leader did even when the event arrives late. Panel wording fixes.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Side by side / Together: Live sync holds its regular poll while a start or stop is due, so followers start on the moment (it could run 100-200 ms into it).

version.author: James
version.changelog: Side by side: a follower stops only after two readings at the leader's stop position (a momentary position glitch stopped one early), and says whether it stopped by position or by time.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Fix 0.9.4: the stop debounce read the project before it was known. check_locals also guards proj/cfg/b/key.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Side by side: an older cue can never replace a newer one (a stale stop swallowed the next start); while playing, Live sync's full pass runs every 2 s (it could stall REAPER ~0.5 s). check_locals guards every script-level variable.

version.author: James
version.changelog: No more UI stutter from status checks: whether Syncthing and the NINJAM server run, and Syncthing's connections, are now checked in the background (they froze REAPER 0.3-0.4 s at every panel refresh).

version.author: James
version.changelog: Background checks run through a hidden-window runner (0.9.7 flashed a console window). The panel warns when ReaNINJAM is sending in Normal or Voice mode, which makes Play along miss the song. A follower that plays along while the leader records says so.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Play along placeholders also work when ReaNINJAM sits on a track instead of the master. Clearer follower message while someone records. Side by side + Play along verified to line up at 0 ms between two machines.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Claim a time selection (shown as a [claimed: you] region; track > time > region > driver). NINJAM's metronome is off for Play along/Listen live, with a toggle. Solo edit: the first checkout opens a copy in its own tab (it used to turn the live session's tab into the copy); restoring a version really reloads it (it silently didn't); a solo tab shows only Solo edit; History groups Solo versions apart; no empty versions.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Break-round fixes: Solo projects save media paths relative (other machines found everything offline) and say when items couldn't be printed; a tempo change no longer reprints every take (rounding), and reprints go two at a time; a moved/trimmed revision also goes out as an edit so History has it; a copy of a bandmate's take is never sent as yours; renaming a track you don't own snaps back and edits keep the band's track name; a print missing from the shared folder is printed again; slivers are skipped out loud; Open session won't open a song twice; snap-back names the owner; plug-in chain names can't collide.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Solo edit prints are keyed by the project as saved (not live plug-in values), so another machine's check-in doesn't reprint unchanged parts. Paste messages fixed; a put-back that can't land exactly no longer repeats every pass.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Review fixes: a change refused because a claim or handover hadn't synced yet waits (up to 10 min) instead of being dropped, and authority is judged by who drove at the time; malformed events/manifests or conflict copies can't stall or repeat; Live sync survives any error in a tick; insert/remove bars applies the map it carries and its edits wait for it (late joiners replay correctly); a take deleted without the right comes back; claims are never wiped by a failed read and keep their own dates, Release mine asks; Solo checkout always takes the newer project and reuses identical prints; safer file replace on Windows; import does one take index per pass.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Taking control no longer shows a dialog (it paused Live sync); time claims show the bars they cover and keep their own date; a bad manifest names what's missing; Syncthing starts from a path with an apostrophe; the Mac installer reports a failed install; README lists the remaining limits.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Claim and take-back labels count bars from the tempo map (the displayed position rounded 4.999 s into the next bar: '2.5-5.0 s' read 'bars 2-3').

version.author: James
version.changelog: Concurrent edits converge: when two people change one take or fader at once, the newest change wins on every machine (a fast clock can't freeze a take). Same-second claims and handovers are decided the same way everywhere. Solo lock conflict copies are tidied on release.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Undoing one of BandSync's own changes no longer gets redone at once (Live sync waits 30 s so you can keep undoing, e.g. back to your own track delete). Your own events count as seen (a clock that ran ahead can't outrank your later changes). Moving a bandmate's take moves its MIDI copy too. Live sync says so when its tab is closed. Solo edit won't open a second tab of a solo copy that's still open.

version.author: James
version.changelog: A take that comes back after a delete you weren't allowed to make is put back as it was here (position, trim, lane, mute), not as it was first sent.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Undoing a delete you sent brings the take back for the band too (its files come out of the trash and an undelete goes out); if it's no longer yours to change, it's removed again with a message.

version.author: James
version.changelog: New: Send selection. Sends what's highlighted: selected items, every item on selected tracks, or everything in a time selection; with a time selection, only its inside (items crossing its edges are split there) or whole items; optionally every take of each item. Works from any project too: pick the song and the takes land there at the same bar and beat (warns when the tempo differs). Replaces Send takes in the panel.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Send selection: the menu (with 'every take of each item') also shows when there's no time selection.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Send selection: nothing is split until you confirm; the dialog says which stretch goes and that outside parts stay; tempo warning only for the stretch sent (and names both tempos); song/room pickers have headers; counts read '1 item (2 takes)'; menus don't jump; no undo point unless something was split.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Side by side is saved with the song (a closed and reopened tab used to come back with it off, so it ignored the band's play/stop). SonoBus rejoins under your BandSync name even if the server renamed you once (e.g. 'Laptop 4').

version.author: James
version.changelog: Installers (from the first real Mac run): the password prompt is explained before it appears; REAPER is asked to close properly (save prompt included) and the installer waits for it, then reopens the project you had open; no 'send the host your ID' when you're already connected; Syncthing's default folder location is only set on a fresh setup.

version.author: James
version.changelog: New song chooser: Open session, Solo edit and Send selection (from another project) open one searchable window instead of a long menu: most recent activity first, with host, who's in it and when, the room picked right there (or a new side room typed in), Enter/Esc, and right-click to hide old or test songs on this machine. Installers sign Tailscale in as a tagged band machine, so it never has to sign in again (the host adds one tagOwners line to the tailnet policy once); a machine whose key expiry was turned off by hand is left alone.

version.author: James
version.changelog: The host lets new band machines into the shared folder by itself when they ask over the band's Tailscale (anything else waits for 'Let in' in the panel's Bandmates). Messages go to a new Activity list in the panel instead of popping the console up. Send selection asks at most one plain question (the part inside the time selection, the whole clips, or everything in those bars), asks about other takes only when a clip has them, and warns when Live sync is off. macOS: background checks and launching Syncthing/NINJAM work again (quoted commands never ran), and the Syncthing check no longer freezes the UI. Installers turn on 'Start Live sync with REAPER' and restart REAPER so your tabs come back.

version.author: James
version.changelog: New: Prepare this project for BandSync (panel: More, and the first screen). A checklist for an already busy project, done after a backup copy as one undo: multi-take items into fixed lanes keeping the playing take, 24-bit FLAC recording at one sample rate, unnamed/duplicate track names, WAV/AIFF converted to FLAC (verified sample by sample, originals kept in 'BandSync originals', 32-bit float left alone), outside files copied in, empty items and slivers removed, ripple editing off, SonoBus on the master, Live sync with REAPER. Chooser and checklist windows are opaque; the autostart toggle no longer reports a false failure.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Song chooser: songs in folders (right-click a song > Move to folder, or a new one; the band sees the same folders), side rooms listed under their song, and who's in older songs taken from who sent takes. Installers: a machine already signed in to Tailscale is left alone (re-signing in with a tag that wasn't allowed yet signed a Mac out and kept failing); a fresh sign-in whose tag is refused clears it and signs in plainly; the tag policy line is shown to the host only. macOS: temporary files go to your own TMPDIR.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Prepare's button is 'Continue'. Publishing a new song from a project that isn't prepared offers the Prepare checklist first (or publish as it is). The panel reloads itself in place when an update lands, and has 'Open another song' (the chooser, opening in a new tab). The chooser says how many songs are hidden. The panel has no collapse arrow (re-expanding came back tiny on macOS). Installers: one request to REAPER per run (a second one arriving while ReaPack's report window was open crashed REAPER on macOS); the setup step waits inside REAPER for ReaPack, and says so plainly if REAPER closed.

version.author: James
version.changelog: macOS installer: a running REAPER with BandSync's background loop gets the setup step as a request file, never an 'open' (any Apple Event while ReaPack's report window is open crashes REAPER); otherwise it first asks you to close ReaPack's windows. Live sync saves the project right after a delete goes out (a crash brought a taken-back take back). Autostart restarts Live sync for every session tab, not only the one in front. Live sync can run for several song tabs without REAPER's 'terminate instances?' box.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Installers: when BandSync is already installed through ReaPack, the setup step leaves ReaPack alone (starting a ReaPack sync while its Transaction report window was open crashed REAPER on macOS); updates come with BandSync - Update. The panel's Activity header keeps its open/closed state and shows long lines cut with '...'.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Hear bandmates' parts Wet, Dry (no effects, whatever plug-ins you have) or Dry + their plug-ins (missing ones stay in the chain, switched off, settings kept), per part or all at once (Together tab). New: Share this sound, which renders a bandmate's dry part through the plug-ins on your copy (theirs or your own) and sends it as an extra take beside theirs on every machine; theirs keeps playing.

version.author: James
version.changelog: New: the mix layer. The driver's effect buses and other tracks without recordings (plug-ins and automation included), the sends from parts into them and the master's plug-ins reach everyone, rebuilt by track name. Dry on a MIDI part plays the notes through the instrument only; a MIDI part's copy takes the part's fader and pan. Share this sound works for MIDI parts, renders the recording once with one fresh tail, and no longer makes BandSync put the original back.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Driver writes, others listen (default): while someone else drives and is here, your changes stay on your machine as scratch instead of going out or being put back (Session > Sync can turn it off). The band's changes wait until you've paused editing (up to 10 s), so none lands mid-drag. New: Undo my last change, which goes back through only your own changes (moves and trims, fader/pan/mute, deletes) from the band's history. Switching wet/dry while playing replays held notes. Share this sound sends the same length and tail as the original, so it fits the item exactly.

version.author: James
version.changelog: End of session: Live sync saves a restore point when it stops (and after 20 quiet minutes) that is kept for good; Empty old trash never removes audio a kept point needs. Google Drive copy of each room: what someone does alone reaches the band whenever they next open the song (deletes and new revisions land in the right place on both sides). Fixes: the mix never carries SonoBus or ReaNINJAM (they hold each machine's name and group password), and a machine's own stay on its master; sends into buses also leave a part's MIDI copy, so Dry modes keep the reverb; Share this sound uses where the item sits now; Undo my last change puts back the exact shape before your change and pressing again steps further back; Live sync and the panel reload themselves after an update.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Fixes: switching a claimed part to Dry no longer mutes that track for the band; Share this sound on a MIDI part keeps its last 2 s; Undo my last change restores the take's start offset correctly; the Google Drive copy no longer leaves Google's ' (1)' duplicates (each machine carries its own files first, others' after 5 minutes) and tidies existing ones.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Fix: Live sync stopped receiving after 0.14.4 machines' edits (their 'previous shape' field clashed with a track's old name); those events are read correctly now.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Alone = full control: with no bandmate in the room, everything you change goes to the band whoever drives or claimed it, and reaches them when they're back; when someone joins, the usual rules return. If two people worked alone at the same time, each keeps their side as a restore point before the other's changes land. The Solo edit tab is gone (its versions stay in History & restore). Panel: a Google Drive copy switch.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Live MIDI view: while a bandmate records MIDI, the notes they play appear on your timeline a few seconds later (a muted placeholder on their '(live)' track, growing as they play; you hear them through Listen live) and give way to their real take when it arrives. Fix: the both-alone restore point is saved whichever side worked alone first.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Same room (Session tab): one switch for Listen live plus side by side with no lag, so everyone hears each other and follows whoever presses play, stop or record. Live MIDI view keeps growing through held notes and pauses, and its placeholders go when the real take arrives (or 15 minutes after, if it never does).

version.author: James
version.changelog: Live MIDI view streams as a new small file every second (one file rewritten twice a second never synced until the recording stopped), so bandmates see the notes while you play.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Live MIDI view: each second's file carries only what changed and none is removed while recording (deleted files were often gone before a bandmate's Syncthing fetched them), so the view reaches bandmates in steps while you play.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Live sync tunes the band folder's Syncthing for live use (changes offered within 2 s even while files keep changing), so the live MIDI view runs about 2 s behind instead of 7. Google Drive copy: someone else's take is filed on Drive by their own machine first (two machines moving it at once made Drive refuse one: 'Can't add file ... permission to add files to takes'), and Drive's '(1)' copies in takes and trash are tidied.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Google Drive copy: each machine writes only its own files there (two machines on one Google account writing the same file made Drive move copies to Lost and Found with 'Can't sync file' messages); everyone still reads everything from it. Live MIDI view no longer redraws a long-finished recording after Live sync reloads.

version.author: James
version.changelog: End-of-session projects: each session's end is also saved as a plain REAPER project in the band's Google Drive (sessions/), opening without BandSync; bandmates' takes are read from the room's Drive copy and your own recordings are copied once, a little at a time. When the driver steps away while others are still here, Live sync says so and the panel offers Take control now (they can take it back when they return).

version.author: James
version.changelog: Google Drive: BandSync looks for Drive at most every 5 minutes and copies every 3 (looking every poll on two machines of one account ran into Drive's rate limit, which held uploads back and caused 'Can't add file' messages). End-of-session projects are plain: SonoBus and ReaNINJAM come out of every track's plug-ins, and BandSync's own session state is left out.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Rooms tab: side rooms as their own project tabs (copy of the room you're in, join with Go there, Come see invites), Send selected to main, and Bring into main (three-way: side-room-only changes come over, clashes listed to pick, per-track ticks, kept restore point first). Plug-ins everyone has: each machine publishes its plug-in names and an FX browser folder 'BandSync (everyone has)' lists what the whole band has. Google Drive: the shared BandSync folder is found in any My Drive and never created. Fixes: a second tab's Live sync never started (each tab now gets a launcher action); closing a tab with Live sync running raised an error box; restore points added a print's tail to its length on every restore; the autostart flag could name the wrong tab after an update.

version.author: James
version.changelog: App look for the panel: top bar (song, room, syncing, driver), sidebar pages (Home with the Same room button and a card per bandmate showing here/recording/driving/armed; Rooms; Together; Live; History; Settings), cards, pills and switches. BandSync - Classic panel (or Settings) keeps the old tabbed layout as a backup. Installers: optional band plug-in pack (Surge XT, Dexed, Airwindows Consolidated, Dragonfly Reverb, Chow Tape Model from their official releases; Saike's and Chokehold's JSFX through ReaPack). Status receipts say who's recording.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Panel: resizes from any edge; Window menu (fill the screen or a half, and back); Dock/Undock; compact layout with a row of pages when short (bottom docker); top bar lined up, with Undo/Redo of your own changes; Maintenance page (red/yellow set-up and health, dismissable yellow, dot on the sidebar); claims and who-changes-what back on Home; Choose who you hear (SonoBus); tooltips on every page and control; the BandSync logo and wordmark; optional system window frame.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Editing modes per room, picked by the driver: Driver only, Claims (default) or Open. A change you may not make is put back instead of being kept on your machine only; a click-through banner at the foot of REAPER's timeline says what you can change while someone else drives. History filters (person, kind of change, track, words) with Restore per change. Full screen button. The logo and name moved to the foot of Maintenance. Fix: the banner text was never shown (assigned before its local declaration).

version.author: James
version.changelog: Tempo and marker changes by someone who isn't driving are put back, like every change they may not make.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Publish sets the 24-bit FLAC recording format itself instead of asking to prepare the project for that alone. Side room names Windows reserves (CON, NUL, COM1...) are refused.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Windows installer: no longer stops right after the plug-in pack (its $plugins folder variable was the -Plugins option, PowerShell names ignore case). Folder installs (-Scripts folder) get the plug-in pack's JSFX repositories too.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Laptop QA fixes: narrow panel (top bar pieces wrap to a second line, text wraps inside cards, button rows wrap, tooltips wrap, combo and name fields fit); Exit full screen only after Full screen; the banner no longer draws over the floating panel; radios and checkboxes visible on cards; 'Hold my changes' everywhere; the Live page says which track ReaNINJAM is on; classic Who changes what reads driver, claims, then Google Drive. Live sync retries Syncthing's folder settings while a Syncthing it just started comes up. Installers say that adding the JSFX runs a full ReaPack sync, and that new plug-ins reach the band list after a REAPER restart.

version.author: James
version.changelog: History: positions read as bars, a group's line opens it with what it was about wrapped under it, restore points and notes wrap. Starting Syncthing looks at the running processes fresh (a 15-second-old list said 'not running' right after a start), and Live sync says plainly if Syncthing didn't start.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Joining a song or side room starts Live sync and logs one line instead of a dialog about naming tracks (they're already there). Top bar: Undo/Redo as arrow icons, the window's buttons at the right end, 'room: main', Start only when Live sync isn't running (Stop is in Settings). Your own take put back reads as the rule, not 'it's James's'. No banner over tabs that aren't band sessions. Clean-up: the Solo edit mix copy and set-up row are gone, the two Solo edit actions are marked older, the installers ask about the band's Google Drive copy instead of Solo edit, and messages name pages that exist in both looks.

version.author: James
version.changelog: A change someone may not make is put back before anything is sent or reprinted (a put-back tempo change no longer reprints MIDI takes twice, and the put-back is immediate). No banner in Open mode.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Put-back messages follow the room's mode: in Driver only they name the driver and say to take control (claims don't help there).

version.author: James
version.changelog: The Undo arrow points the right way (it was drawn upside down).

version.author: James
version.changelog: Docked wide (a bottom docker): each page's parts stand side by side as columns, scrolling sideways when they don't fit; the page tabs sit in the top row; Same room comes first and bandmates are one line each. Bring into main: notes compared by their own fingerprint and only when the room was made on this machine (every MIDI take looked edited), labels say what changed (moved, muted, trimmed), changes on tracks someone else claimed are shown as 'can't bring' and left out, the preview list grows with the page. History says muted/unmuted/trimmed/moved. Undo and Redo arrows are exact mirrors. Rooms page: a one-line description, details on hover. Window menu: Move to the next screen.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Undo this: undo a single change from History. Selected tracks to here: put only the selected tracks back to a History change or recall point. Only one Live sync per tab (a newer one takes over). Docked: more columns, a 'more below' marker, a hint when the docker is short. Maintenance dot explains itself.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Docked: the 'more below' strip now hides what's under it; recall points put their words under the buttons when narrow.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Autostart reloads itself on updates (no more restart attempts after dialogs once REAPER has restarted once). Restore counts only takes that changed. Docked: History rows put the change above its buttons, recall points fill the column, Live shows Mode and Server side by side, 'more below' fades the cut-off line, clearer hint.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Docked: History's changes scroll with the column (reachable at the default docker height); 'more below' is its own line under each column, never over text; the read-only banner sits clear of the docker's splitter.

version.author: James
version.changelog: The panel reopens with REAPER when it was open at close (Autostart; closing its window turns that off). Docked: 'more below' only when a column really hides something.

version.author: James
version.changelog: The panel opens by itself whenever a BandSync session opens (once per opening: closed, it stays closed until the next one). With the panel closed, an edit that gets put back says why in a tooltip by the mouse.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Put-back messages say whose take it is ("James's take on Keys"), not the take's id.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Mirror sync: every machine in a room holds the same project (tracks, items, lanes, MIDI, plug-in chains, copies, unnamed tracks). History restores the project, the selected tracks, or one change. New pages: Play, Chat, Plugins (translations), Setup. Publish needs Prepare, saves untitled projects, keeps a copy from before BandSync. Bigger plug-in pack with an extras option. Songs from older versions must be published again.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Radial menu: a ring at the mouse for undo, redo, the three History restores, take control, Real time mode and chat. MIDI prints no longer stop on REAPER's 'file already exists' warning. Leftover take machinery removed from sync; Live sync skips the mirror scan when nothing changed.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Reopening a project without its last save (closed unsaved, or a crash) no longer brings its tracks and items back twice for the band: they get their ids back and catch up with the band.

version.author: James
version.changelog: The History page is now called Restore (links and the radial menu follow).

version.author: James
version.changelog: Automation envelopes and sends between tracks now sync (what you show or arm stays yours). Plug-ins, automation and sends land when the song's tab is in front: REAPER broke sends when a track was rewritten in a tab behind. Pooled MIDI copies no longer show up as a difference between machines.

version.author: James
version.changelog: More of each track syncs: width and pan mode, channel count, the FX button, the master/parent send, timebase, playback offset, groups/VCA, lock, input FX and MIDI note names. The song's title, notes, group names and timebase travel with the tempo map. Opening or moving a take plug-in's window is no longer a change.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Every blind spot closed: the master track's plug-ins and automation, automation items, ruler lanes, Melodyne edits (as prints), files plug-ins load, freeze. Solo and item grouping stay each person's own. Grey stand-ins for audio still arriving. BandSync - Undo / Redo actions for Ctrl+Z. Change your name in Setup > Options. Open session previews a song's size and missing plug-ins. A reopened older save no longer brings back tracks the band deleted. Licensed GPL-3.0-or-later.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Edit holds: what a bandmate is changing is theirs for 15 seconds. Follow a bandmate's view; Ping here in the radial menu. A BandSync category in the FX browser. Undo no longer counts BandSync's own print refreshes as your change. Your own changes aren't listed as from the band. Track colours stay put when BandSync adds or removes a track.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Draw on the tracks for everyone (Chat > Draw on the tracks). Plug-in chains no longer read as different after loading on a bandmate's machine. Prints are refreshed only by someone who may change the item. New actions appear in the Actions list after an update by themselves. Clearer 'sent' messages for project settings.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Live sync waits while the mouse button is down: a band change no longer lands mid-drag and undoes it, and a drag skipped by the look for changes is looked at again after the drop.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Drawings: one colour per person (no two people in a room share one), and a stroke no longer stores the same point over and over. A ping now tells whoever sent it that it went out.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Real time mode: a hear / muted button per bandmate (each gets their own SonoBus output pair, mixed by BandSync live mix on your master); My time / Their time; a Guest mode for someone with only SonoBus, with Measure their delay (clap along to 8 clicks) and Line up their takes. SonoBus is checked to have joined the band's group, retried twice, then you're told. A server-renamed 'Laptop 5' counts as you; only one SonoBus per machine stays in the group. The Real time track no longer recolours the band's tracks. 246 lines of unused code removed.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Real time mode's controls wrap onto the next line in a narrow (docked) panel instead of being cut off: the hear button, Guest, Configure SonoBus. 'Their time (my backing later)' says whose side moves, and switching it is logged.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Guest: measure right before you record. Tested PC to laptop over SonoBus on Wi-Fi, the round trip drifted 426-555 ms within two minutes as SonoBus adjusted its buffers; the tooltip, log and README say so.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Fixes 0.33.2's panel page (a broken string stopped Real time mode's controls loading). tools/compile_check.py now compiles every file before a release.

version.author: James
version.changelog: The panel survives an error inside a card (it shows the error instead of closing); the hear button hides while Real time mode is off; someone has to be gone 90 s (not 45) before you get full control, so a dialog left open on their machine no longer flips it.

version.author: James
version.changelog: An item with a VST take FX no longer makes the projects differ for good (its 'Program 1' line is left out of the comparison, as for track FX). After you undo, the band's changes wait up to 30 s, so your redo still works. A handover no longer logs 'moved/trimmed nil'.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Restore brings tracks back in their order (a track whose neighbour came back too no longer jumps to the top, out of its folder). A file in the band's folder that can't be read is skipped for good after 2 minutes, so 'still to come' doesn't stick at 1. A second tab of a song that's already syncing says so instead of offering Start, and Live sync won't start in it. The drawings no longer crash after switching to a non-BandSync tab.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Put-backs say whose it is: 'it's claimed by James: ask them to release it', or 'Laptop drives: claim it, or take control' (it told the driver to take control). A clash within seconds says 'at the same moment as you', not 'while you were apart'.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Mac: the installer no longer stops after its questions; it shows a disk image's licence, takes ~/ and dragged-in folders, asks you to quit REAPER (no Apple Event), waits for Tailscale's extension, detects Apple Silicon under Rosetta. Both installers add js_ReaScriptAPI and SWS. Drawing works on a Mac (its screen y grows upwards). SonoBus is its VST3 only. Syncthing.app is started through the app. Chat links are quoted safely. Shared media names are plain characters.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Correctness round from the code review. A bandmate asking to join shows on every page (Let them in / Not my bandmate). An undone edit stays in a yellow bar until dismissed, and the small button says so. Edits made while you're alone are no longer undone on your own machine. A change that looks refused here waits a minute and then lands (judged by today's claims and dropped after 10 minutes, it left a machine differing for good). A project that has differed from a caught-up bandmate's for a minute brings itself in line with the band's newest version. Full disks no longer leave cut-off files; copies go a piece at a time and are checked. Your unsent changes (settling, playing, Hold my changes) are no longer replaced by the band's. An item moved onto a track of your own is no longer deleted for everyone. Restore and Undo pick the version the band really had after a clash. Changes for a deleted track no longer wait for ever. A comp keeps its playing take when the band's change arrives. Two computers using one name are told so.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Speed: a look for changes takes 0.06 s instead of 0.46 s at 60 tracks and 2,000 items (unchanged tracks and items aren't worked out again). Catching up on a long history applies only each object's newest revision, finds items through an index and spreads the work over passes (2,020 changes: 1 s). Reading the band's files is about 100 times faster (2.7 MB in 0.02 s), and starting up no longer reads every change in the song.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Open editing now lets anyone change the tempo map, markers and project settings too. A claim follows its track when it's renamed (and you can rename a track you claimed). The driver can release the claims of someone who isn't here; they're told when they're back.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Installers ask 'Is someone in the band already set up?' (any set-up bandmate's Syncthing ID will do) instead of 'are you the host': a host is a song's, not a machine's. On a Mac, arrow keys edit the answers, and a name with accents is shown cleaned (or said) instead of changed silently. Local mixing off and Take control ask with named choices (as Yes/No, 'No' sent your faders to everyone). Deleting a chat message for everyone asks first.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Mac joins now match Windows (plug-in file names and colours hashed the same; track and marker colours travel in one byte order). Start screen leads with Join the band's song; Restore has Undo on every change; Real time, saved versions and plain editing-mode names; listening controls on Play. Sync pill, Holding N changes, Armed together warning, REAPER version check, Render the final mix, Invite a bandmate. Installer installs SonoBus, Tailscale and Drive, waits for sign-ins, shows the ID format, updates an old BandSync. docs/clashes.md.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Catching up on a big burst of changes is several times faster (passes come back in 0.3 s while changes wait; files read once). The sync pill no longer counts your own changes as Receiving. Undo says You changed it after this; undo entries name the track as it is now; the chooser starts on the newest song. Google Drive with several accounts: the one holding the band's folder is used (installer and panel), Health says when it's signed out, and the Mac's shortcut symlink is found. The invite line skips the set-up question; short installer prompts. An old drift note clears once everyone matches.

version.author: James
version.changelog: MIDI takes are named dry and wet (keeping their name after a dash); MIDI plays as Auto / Dry / Wet. When the band deletes a whole track, its items no longer show false 'isn't yours to delete' put-backs. The sync pill just says Sending; Who's here shows who is still getting changes. Setup shows which Google account the Drive copy goes to.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Per-song sync: every computer gets every song's listing, and a song in full once it's opened there, so a new bandmate's first sync isn't the whole library. Setup > Options > Songs on this computer: Stop downloading a song, or Keep every song (for the machine that stays on). Computers that already had songs keep them. The installers set this up for new bandmates. The Update button says to try again if GitHub hasn't caught up.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Per-song sync: songs already here count by their takes, media, changes or stems (0.34.7 counted changes only, so older songs with takes but no changes stopped updating on machines that had them; each machine checks again once).

version.author: James
version.changelog: Opening a song whose history arrives out of order (a track deleted and later brought back) no longer loses that track's items: once the track is back, every change that hadn't landed is put in place.

version.author: James
version.changelog: The start screen names the song worked on last (as the song chooser does). Setup > Health no longer shows 'Live sync is off' for a few seconds after another tab closes.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Bands: each band is its own shared folder with its own songs, bandmates, plug-ins and Drive copy. Start a band and switch bands in Setup > Options > Bands; song tabs keep their own band. Invite a bandmate invites to the band you're in, and Let them in shares only that band; any bandmate's panel now shows Let them in, not only the host's. The installer names a new band and joins the invited one.

version.author: James
version.changelog: A bandmate already in one of your bands who joins another of them (their installer offers that band's folder) shows up with Let them in, which shares just that band's folder.

version.author: James
version.changelog: The panel follows a band switch made elsewhere (an installer joining a band); a song tab from before bands finds its own band by its song, and the top bar never says 'nil drives'. The installer leaves BandSync alone when this version already runs from the band folder (no second ReaPack copy), and installs Neural Amp Modeler on Windows through the installer inside its zip.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Drawing gets a toolbar: Pen, Highlighter, Line, Arrow, Box, Text and Eraser, a colour, a size (S, M, L) and Undo (your last drawing). Drawings made before still show as pen strokes.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Drawing: quick clicks and fast drags register where you pressed; the toolbar sits at the foot on a dark backing with Done, Undo and Clear mine in fixed places; the eraser finds a box by its edges and text by its words; text follows the size; the highlighter is one smooth stroke; envelope lanes count as their track; the mouse wheel zooms and scrolls while drawing; colours no one has as their own.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Drawing: Undo takes one drawing per click again; the dark swatch has an outline; a colour from 0.35.3 falls back to yours; the hint ignores the track under the toolbar; Top/Bottom moves the toolbar.

version.author: James
version.changelog: MIDI that plays an instrument on another track (a MIDI send to a sampler or kit track) gets a wet print rendered through that track, with only that item feeding it. Where that instrument doesn't load, the print plays and Setup > Health names what's missing.

version.author: James
version.changelog: A routed MIDI track's send to its instrument carries MIDI only once it's printed, so Wet doesn't play the print twice. Print files carry who rendered them, so two machines' prints of one item never collide (Syncthing couldn't replace one REAPER had open).

version.author: James
version.changelog: A big burst of your changes goes out a quarter second at a time, so REAPER no longer freezes for seconds while it's sent. Old history is trimmed once a day by the room's driver: changes older than 30 days that no major saved version needs go to a local archive. History hides prints BandSync refreshed by itself and names tempo/marker changes plainly; the song list shows people by their current names; the Back to here menu explains itself without a tooltip over it.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Live sync starts with REAPER again for a project reopened under a differently written path. A song the band deletes now leaves every computer, including the parts per-song sync wasn't downloading.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Track colours travel between bandmates (except from a computer with SWS auto-colouring on). Every song on your computer keeps a copy on the band's Google Drive, recordings included, so a song opens even when nobody who has it is online. History the trim removed no longer comes back from Drive. On Windows the plug-in pack installs without setup windows, with one permission prompt.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Prints now render in the background in a hidden second REAPER, so you can keep working. Audio on a track with a plug-in a bandmate lacks gets a wet take like MIDI does. While a wet take plays, its track's plug-ins are switched off on that computer, so effects don't apply twice. Prints leave out the item's own volume and fades. SWS auto-colouring is switched off while a band song is in front.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Everyone has a colour: pick your own or keep a default. Tracks can show who is editing or has claimed them, or whose track each one is (Setup > Options); that only changes this computer. Background prints now run on a hidden Windows desktop, so nothing flashes or takes the keyboard, and routed MIDI prints render in the background too. Fixed routed prints picking up other tracks, and a track colour that differed between computers.

version.author: James
version.changelog: If whoever changed a part lacks its plug-ins, a bandmate in the song who has them prints it, and Print selected tracks here puts you in charge of printing a track. Takes become lanes in band songs, keeping your comp. Setup > Options can switch background rendering off. Your own startup scripts no longer run in the hidden render REAPER, and its copy of the song is no longer marked as a band song.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Mac: background rendering finds REAPER now, and is off by default because a second REAPER takes the keyboard there (it can be switched on in Setup > Options). A colour someone else shows in can't be picked any more, so a pick doesn't move a bandmate's default.

version.author: James
version.changelog: A computer missing a JS plug-in no longer prints silent wet takes: REAPER keeps missing JSFX as an empty stand-in, so BandSync now checks the file is really there. MIDI sent to a JS instrument on another track (chmaha's drum kits, organ, pianos) prints through it. The Mac tidies leftover render folders.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Claims on tracks that were deleted or renamed are let go automatically, and aren't listed meanwhile. When takes become lanes, the lanes are named Take 1, Take 2 beside the comp lane.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Background prints run with a settings folder of their own: your plug-ins and effects, but none of REAPER's extensions, MIDI devices or control surfaces, and your reaper.ini and Recent projects are left alone. Prints come out faster too.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Going back to something already printed (an undo, a note put back) reuses its print at once instead of rendering it again in front. Background prints go in as soon as they're done. Old render folders are cleared away.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Going back to something a bandmate already printed uses their print at once, instead of rendering your own copy.

version.author: James
version.changelog: A track you make is claimed for you and shows on the Claims card; a maker no longer beats a bandmate's claim. Selecting notes and opening the MIDI editor are no longer changes, and undoing a hand edit reuses the old print. New option: open bandmates' MIDI edits as they happen.

version.author: James
version.changelog: One Ctrl+Z now undoes your own edit: reading your own change back no longer adds a BandSync undo step on top of it. A bandmate shows as settling, not a red project differs, for the normal seconds after an edit.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Wet takes in a burst: a part renders once it has held still for 3 s, up to three at once, longest-waiting first, and a render of a version that's gone is ended. Each background render has its own settings, which fixes a rare hang on a plug-in scan nobody could see.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Printing a part you had selected no longer adds an Unselect all items undo step above your edit, so one Ctrl+Z reaches it after a rendered print too.

version.author: James
version.changelog: A finished wet take goes out on the next pass instead of waiting up to 10 s.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Background renders on a Mac: on by default, nothing shows and nothing takes the keyboard. They run from a private background copy of REAPER, made on first use, with windows kept transparent. Macs also end outdated renders now.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Plug-ins that change their saved data by themselves (Kilohearts Disperser) no longer stop a track syncing or printing: BandSync says so once and goes by their knobs. Wet takes arrive sooner, as BandSync looks every half second while one is on its way.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Moving a knob on a plug-in that changes its saved data by itself now renders a new wet take.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Limit-testing fixes. A computer without a plug-in no longer prints silence or plays silent notes. Background renders wait for sample instruments to load, and a stuck plug-in no longer blocks REAPER. Deleted tracks come back with their parts; side rooms respect claims; fixes a freeze on every log line, and new tabs left with Live sync off.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Fixes a track-order loop where put-back tracks kept going out. Track order differences no longer read as a different project. A part left on silent notes moves to its wet take on opening. Big songs are looked at less often while prints are on their way.

version.author: James
version.changelog: From playing a real song together. Comps on played parts become lanes and reach the band. Volume automation is no longer printed into wet takes and applied again. Plug-ins that save their data their own way no longer make computers disagree or trigger re-renders. Opening a song you've been in goes back to your own project. Send selected brings a new track's plug-ins. Page tabs stay put, and notices stay with their song.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Comping again on a track in lanes keeps the track playing. Going back never removes what a bandmate added since, and what you removed comes back on the way forward. The whole song going back includes tempo and markers. The driver can hand over from the panel.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Comp a second time keeps the track playing. Restore: Back never takes a bandmate's new work, forward keeps lane names, tempo goes back too, claims wait out a Back and forward, one act shows as one row. Lane collapse stays your own. Passes on lanes nobody hears aren't printed. Fingerprints compare by the band's newest change, so a plug-in that saves its data differently on each machine no longer shows as different. No empty plug-in chain goes out for a track just back.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Fixes a loop after a whole-song Back that grew a track to 256 lanes and re-sent its items over and over. A track never has fewer lanes than its items sit on, a nonsense lane number is rejected, and adding a lane no longer counts as a change to every item. Comping: every print is removed before takes become lanes, only on the items being split, and the part you played over moves to its own lane.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Going Back no longer sends the same tracks dozens of times: tracks whose saved places pointed at each other went out 73 times each and stopped REAPER for seconds.

version.author: James
version.changelog: A reopened file waits until it has caught up before its takes become lanes. Undoing a glue also takes the glued part away; one act is one row in Restore. Bring into main follows claims. Side rooms can be binned and brought back. The final mix tells you if it reaches full scale. Fixes plug-in chains left waiting for good after a Back.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Adding a track no longer sends or puts back tracks you never touched: what moved is worked out from the whole list. Forward takes back what going back revived after a bandmate's delete, so a glue doesn't end up doubled. Restore's Undo says when it undoes several changes, and one act is one row in the full list too.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Ctrl+Z never rolls back a bandmate's work in a band song: your own edit on top of REAPER's list undoes as ever, a band change on top undoes your own last change instead. Set by itself on Windows at the next REAPER start, or with the button in Set up; regular projects behave as always. Redo no longer undoes your last change when there's nothing to redo, and a print finishing doesn't clear it. Tracks restored by Back no longer go out because of their place in the list.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z now work while the BandSync panel has focus, except while you're typing in a text box, which keeps its own undo.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Restore's Undo groups an act's changes only on the same lane, and rows name their lane: deleting a pass and its copies in the comp gives you a row for each, so bringing back the pass doesn't bring old comp pieces with it. A glue still undoes as one.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Restore's rows name a lane as it was called when the change was made, so old rows stay right after lanes are added or removed.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Restore has two buttons: Render current mix puts the whole song, as your master has it, in the shared folder and on Drive; Back up keeps a saved version for good and the project on Drive. Saving a project to Drive no longer stops REAPER for most of a minute.

version.author: James
version.changelog: On Windows, REAPER starts without stopping at Replace missing file or Project Load Warning for band songs: BandSync opens them itself and says in Activity what's missing. Dock > Left or Right works with no right-click, and Undock returns to the usual size. A lane that holds little of a track says so. A part with only its print no longer turns the track's plug-ins off. Take control asks one question. Side rooms don't re-print what hasn't changed in them. Twenty quiet minutes no longer saves an 'end of session'. Reopening picks the project last worked on. A 14th-digit change after a tempo map isn't sent.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Suggestions: an edit reaching someone's claim goes to them as one Accept or Decline, and the claim never moves. A tempo change is nobody's edit. A bus holding someone's claim can't be deleted, and a change to one says whose parts it affects. A copy of a claimed track goes out as yours, with credit. Mac: Dock no longer crashes, and the Cmd+Z row shows on Setup.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Suggestion and undone lines show their buttons first, so a panel docked short can reach them. A wet take on a lane that isn't playing no longer takes the track's plug-ins off. Render's tooltip no longer reads as if your own parts are left out.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Undoing an accepted suggestion no longer reloads plug-ins, which re-printed Superior Drummer's parts. A (yours, not sent) track left empty goes on its own.

version.author: James
version.changelog: For every kind of remote collaborator: groups, projects and collaborators replace bands, songs and bandmates. Minimize sits by the close button and the small button drags from anywhere, with Lock position. Claims show under each person in Who's here. Rooms: click the square, Create side room asks for a name, archived rooms in a dropdown. Open project: a folder view, and each project catches up as it opens. The Chat page no longer lags, Draw is a toggle, Hide drawings works, drawings show for everyone without asking, and everything filters by collaborator. Restore: a radio for each kind of change, and Open in side room.

version.author: James

version.author: James
version.changelog: A VCA fader counts as a bus: moving one says whose parts it affects, and one leading someone's claimed track can't be deleted.

version.author: James
version.changelog: KitchenSync on screen (working title). Restore: click a change for its options, old filter back. A small square for Minimize. Coloured pills, themes (Dark, Light, Midnight, Warm). Fixes for cut-off layouts. A VCA or lock on someone's track goes back here and goes to them as a suggestion. Undoing a comp's leftover row no longer doubles the piece. After a crash REAPER reopens the group's songs with no boxes to answer. Saved after a big catch-up.

version.changelog: Remove someone from a group: Remove on their card (driver or song host), a minute to change your mind, then every computer stops syncing with theirs. A track that only moved in the list is no longer put back and suggested to its owner after a restart.

version.changelog: The small square drags again. Restore whole project in a side room keeps the room's tempo, where it went to the song's first map. Create in the new side room box keeps the typed name.

A warning keeps the top line even when a count lands in the same moment. Restore's words box finds lane names. Expanded groups read newest first. Restore sends no tempo event when the tempo didn't change.

The radial menu stays on the screen. Suggestion buttons wait a moment after the list changes, so a moving row can't take a click.

version.changelog: The name on screen and in the installer's wording is now StudioSync. A removed computer that keeps asking is shown as that, not as someone new. Not my collaborator really dismisses a request. After suggestion rows change, the page below waits a moment too, so a moved button can't take a click. Setup warns if REAPER takes media offline when another app is in front. Tests: a real join, removal and rejoin with a second Syncthing, and band changes on pooled MIDI parts.
